name: Macintosh Laryngoscope Blade
summary: A curved laryngoscope blade designed to be inserted into the vallecula to indirectly lift the epiglottis, facilitating visualization of the glottic opening during endotracheal intubation.

name: Rapid sequence intubation
summary: Rapid sequence intubation is an advanced airway management technique utilizing near-simultaneous administration of a sedative and a neuromuscular blocker to rapidly secure the airway while minimizing the risk of pulmonary aspiration.

name: Preoxygenation
summary: The process of replacing functional residual capacity nitrogen with oxygen to increase the duration of safe apnea during rapid sequence intubation.

name: Fentanyl
summary: Fentanyl is a highly potent, short-acting synthetic piperidine opioid that acts on mu-opioid receptors for the management of severe acute pain and procedural sedation.

name: Etomidate
summary: Etomidate is a short-acting intravenous sedative-hypnotic agent commonly used for rapid sequence intubation and procedural sedation due to its favorable hemodynamic stability.
bnf_dosage:
Induction of anaesthesia

[BY SLOW INTRAVENOUS INJECTION]
• Adult: 150–300 micrograms/kg (max. per dose 60 mg), to be administered over 30-60 seconds (60 seconds in patients in whom hypotension might be hazardous)
• Elderly: 150–200 micrograms/kg (max. per dose 60 mg), to be administered over 30-60 seconds (60 seconds in patients in whom hypotension might be hazardous)

name: Propofol
summary: Propofol is a rapid-onset, short-acting intravenous sedative-hypnotic agent frequently utilized for procedural sedation and the induction of general anesthesia in emergency medicine.
bnf_dosage:

name: Ketamine
summary: A rapid-acting dissociative anesthetic and analgesic used in emergency medicine for procedural sedation, induction for rapid sequence intubation, and management of severe pain.
bnf_dosage:
Induction and maintenance of anaesthesia for short procedures

[BY INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION]
PATIENT AND CARER ADVICE
• Adult: Initially 6.5–13 mg/kg, adjusted according to response, a dose of 10 mg/kg usually produces 12–25 minutes of surgical anaesthesia

[BY INTRAVENOUS INJECTION]
• Adult: Initially 1–4.5 mg/kg, adjusted according to response, to be administered over at least 60 seconds, a dose of 2 mg/kg usually produces 5–10 minutes of surgical anaesthesia
Diagnostic manoeuvres and procedures not involving intense pain

[BY INTRAMUSCULAR INJECTION]
• Adult: Initially 4 mg/kg
• Adult: Initially 0.5–2 mg/kg, using an infusion solution containing 1 mg/ml; maintenance 10–45 micrograms/kg/minute, adjusted according to response

name: Gum Elastic Bougie
summary: A flexible, semi-rigid, single-use stylet used as a blind or visual aid to facilitate endotracheal intubation, particularly in cases of difficult or unanticipated airway anatomy.

name: Laryngeal mask airway
summary: A laryngeal mask airway (LMA), also known as laryngeal mask, is a medical device that keeps a patient's airway open during anaesthesia or while they are unconscious.

name: Mechanical ventilation
summary: Mechanical ventilation or assisted ventilation is the medical term for using a ventilator machine to fully or partially provide artificial ventilation.

name: Trachea
summary: The trachea is a cartilaginous tube connecting the larynx to the bronchi that serves as the primary conduit for airflow to and from the lungs.

name: Cricothyroid membrane
summary: The cricothyroid membrane is an anatomical structure connecting the cricoid and thyroid cartilages that serves as the primary surgical access point during an emergency cricothyrotomy.

name: Glottis
summary: The glottis is the critical anatomical region of the larynx containing the vocal cords and the rima glottidis, serving as the primary landmark for endotracheal intubation and airway management.

name: Thyroid Gland
summary: The thyroid gland is a butterfly-shaped endocrine structure in the neck that secretes triiodothyronine (T3), thyroxine (T4), and calcitonin to regulate systemic metabolism, growth, and calcium homeostasis.
